Updated By Richard Cowan October 11, 2005 7:45PM

Thanks to the great work of attorney Douglas Hiatt, things are looking much better for Steve.

Doug went with Steve to his first federal hearing today, and will accompany him again when Steve will have to appear another federal hearing to determine how he will return to California to face charges for growing medical marijuana.

It will also be determined how the federal charges for Interstate Flight to Avoid Prosecution will be handled.

He has been moved to the federal detention center at Seatac, where he should be getting at least minimal health care tonight. Nonetheless, the brutal way in which Steve has been treated since he was taken from the ER in Vancouver by cowardly little thugs has demonstrated all too clearly the real reason that Steve fled.

Steve fled to NOT to avoid prosecution but rather to avoid being treated precisely the way he really was treated! He wanted to avoid being deprived of the pain relievers to which he is entitled by law!

This morning, Doug Hiatt wrote, I am ashamed. I have met a very small man with a very large heart. Thirteen back surgeries.  He is a sixteen year chronic pain morphine user

He is a medical cannabis user. He has an enlarged prostate and a partially blocked bowel. He is sitting in jail.

As of this writing he has received no pain medication. He kicked hard in the drunk tank in Whatcom county. When I saw him last night he was in tears from the pain. I have contacted the chief jail doctor, Ben Sanders, and notified him of all the above and other relevant medical information. I hope something is done.

Needless to say, this makes me sick...  

More later,

Douglas

I cannot begin to say enough good things about Doug Hiatt.

Steve's story has begun to resonate with the American people and when it is finally told, there will be outrage on both sides of the US/Canadian border.  

I was interviewed about Steve by Dean Becker on the 4:20 Drug War NEWS (MP3 audio)
See
www.endprohibition.org

 

Posted by Richard Cowan October 8, 2005
See
 Steve Tuck Taken from Vancouver ER In Handcuffs to US Border. Will the Feds Kill Him?

Updated October 10, 2005 8:30 Pacific time

I spoke to Steve at 3PM this afternoon. He was finally able to call me after two days in the Seattle Correctional Facility, the King County Jail. During this time he has not been able to make any phone calls. I immediately arranged to have attorneys call and visit the jail.

I have just talked to Doug Hiatt from Jeff Steinborn's law firm, one of the great NORML lawyers who is trying to help. He visited with Steve and is pressing for the jail to provide him with proper medical care. Although your calls and emails certainly got their attention in Whatcom County, Doug thinks it would be best to wait on a new round of protests. The Feds will probably pick Steve up in the morning to move him to California. At that time we will have to be especially vigilant about his medical care. He is in a very weak condition but Doug says that he gained strength when he heard how many people he has looking out for him.

The Feds had dumped him there apparently until they can move him to California. They easily could have taken him to the federal detention center at SEATAC, but apparently chose to try to hide him in the Seattle jail. When the lawyers called the Feds they would neither confirm or deny that they even had him and professed not to know where he was. (Sort of like Osama??)

I had hoped that if he were in Federal custody he would at least be given some medical care, but they did this to punish him for his many friends having called the Whatcom County jail.

The facility in Seattle is much better than in Whatcom. Nonetheless, he has still not been given any morphine or pain relievers of any kind, despite being in such serious condition that he was in the ER in Vancouver.

He is a severely disabled veteran who has has thirteen back surgeries. He even has a metal plate in his lower back. He is in constant pain and needs very large quantities of morphine, especially when he is denied cannabis. As noted, he was taken from the ER in Vancouver where they had given him a permanent catheter. It is now infected. Because his prostate is so enlarged, the attending ER physician wrote on his chart that he needs to see a urologist, ASAP. He is also suffering from blocked bowels. 

Many thanks to NORML and everyone else who have been helping.

Please stand by so that we can be ready once again to demand justice and basic human decency for Steve.

 

He said that he is being denied the use of morphine and being given only a minor pain reliever, so he is in agony from the pain, full-blown morphine withdrawal and terrified.

He said that he had been taken to the hospital, and they said that there was nothing wrong with him, and he did not need more pain medication. The Canadian Border Service officers who took him from the ER were given copies of letters from his American doctors, one three page letter described his history of back surgeries, and others emphasized his need for proper pain medication. One also described his need for cannabis.

Of course, we have no way of knowing whether he was allowed to give them to authorities. In any case, his condition should be obvious to any competent physician. I am frankly astonished by this medical neglect because it is not in the interest of Whatcom County to be sued.

He was also told that he is to be turned over to the Federal authorities but not until Tuesday. We have no idea what the federal indictment may be, but Federal involvement was indicated by the behavior of the Canadian officials and their long-term collaboration with the DEA to violate Steves rights while he was in Canada.

Update: Steve has already been taken by the Feds. He may get better medical care and we are trying to find out what is going to happen to him. There is no further need to contact Whatcom County.

Unfortunately, this also means that he will never be allowed to use cannabis.

His life is in great danger!

Steve asked me, Why are they doing this to me?

I could only tell him that they crucified Jesus. They still are.

He cried, "Please help me!"

Pray for Steve, and God help us all!
